beats.text: The first handheld mobile call was made from a Manhattan pavement.
beats.note: Martin Cooper of Motorola stood on Sixth Avenue near the Hilton and rang Joel Engel, a rival at AT&T.

beats.text: The phone only worked through one base station.
beats.note: Motorola's base station sat on the roof of Burlington House and was hardwired to the AT&T landline network.

beats.context: The recharge time for about 30 minutes of talk. Cooper joked that you could not hold the phone up for that long.

beats.note: Motorola unveiled the DynaTAC 8000X on 6 March 1983. Quantity production began in early April 1984.

beats.text: The first commercial handset cost US$3,995 in 1984.
beats.note: Motorola's own forecast in 1973 had been full operation within three years.

beats.text: His first call went to his chief competitor.
